item.title: USB Gym: A Gymnasium Testbed for Closed-Loop Ultrasound View Matching
item.description:
arXiv Query: search_query=all:ultrasound AND all:segmentation&id_list=&start=0&… · score 0.48

Background and Objective: Our main goal is ultrasound guidance: moving a probe until its image matches a target view. Published methods for each part of a guide are evaluated in separate simulators. We asked whether these methods, combined into one guide, are good enough. Methods: We built USB Gym, a testbed whose standard engine simulates ultrasound from public patient CT, with a network drawing organ textures from CT labels. item.title: Risk Control Certifies Rates, Not Magnitudes: An Audit of Selective Fetal Biometry
item.description:
arXiv Query: search_query=all:ultrasound AND all:segmentation&id_list=&start=0&… · score 0.41

Prenatal ultrasound biometry must return a head circumference (HC) and refuse when the image cannot support one. Selective prediction trades coverage against error, but its finite-sample guarantees bound the rate of gross errors, not their magnitude. We audit a tool-grounded biometry pipeline on two separately pre-registered four-way splits of the 999 labelled HC18 images, retraining the segmenter three times on each. item.title: Task-Aware Bitrate Thresholds for Codec-Robust Ultrasound Segmentation
item.description:
arXiv Query: search_query=all:ultrasound AND all:segmentation&id_list=&start=0&… · score 0.39

Remote robot surgery and tele-ultrasound increasingly rely on real-time streaming under strict bandwidth constraints, making lossy compression unavoidable. Since the receiving end of these clinical pipelines is increasingly a machine rather than a human observer, codec selection must be guided by downstream task accuracy rather than perceptual fidelity. We evaluate three widely deployed codecs, H.264/AVC, HEVC, and AV1, on prostate ultrasound segmentation, reporting task-aware compression performance with region overlap (Dice) and boundary accuracy (HD95) as the quality metrics.
